reporting_issues.note: The abstract prints the systolic pressure changes with beats/min after each value; Table II has them in mm Hg.

The order of the printed pair is as the card describes. One qualification: in Table II the 0.5 mg/kg d-condition carries no marker for a significant difference from 0.5 mg/kg l-methamphetamine on visual-analogue intoxication or drug liking, so the abstract's wording holds for peak values; what the Results report as significantly smaller (P<.0001) is the across-time comparison.
The abstract's version (d 30% smaller) is the one consistent with the ratio.
Verified on the rendered page 411: 4.9 (SD 1.8) with 95% CI 4.9-7.6.
The same legend appears on Figure 5 (p. 415) as well as Figures 4 (p. 413) and 6 (p. 416); all three show dispersion for only the two 0.5 mg/kg conditions.

risk_of_bias.note: Overall some-concerns equals the worst domain, as METHODS 5.3 requires. Design (human-laboratory) and instrument (RoB 2) fit: this is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, Latin-square crossover, the clearest case for RoB 2 among the five cards.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: Randomization process (Latin-square allocation of the six conditions)
risk_of_bias_domains.note: A balanced Latin square is stated (p. 406) without sequence generation or concealment.

Judgment is right (one week between sessions, nothing detectable pre-dose, p. 408). Note that this is an added domain: RoB 2's five domains place carryover under the randomization domain and its crossover extension, so the editor may want the domain renamed rather than added.
Matched volumes, blinding integrity untested; some-concerns fits.
All 12 completed all six sessions; under 1% replaced by the group mean.
Enantioselective assay and automated cardiovascular measurement against unverified blinding of self-reports.
No protocol; roughly forty peak outcomes with uncorrected pairwise tests.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial is right, but the strongest ground is the step from single intravenous doses in 12 men to a prediction about the abuse liability of a market supply and about toxicity under repeated dosing (pp. 418-419), not the abstract's description of the subjective comparison, which holds for peak values (see reporting issue 1).

missed: Funding field is wrong: p. 419 carries an explicit statement that the authors report no conflict of interest; the card records that the article has no conflict-of-interest statement. The Merck fellowship and the ALZA affiliation are correctly noted.

Two further Table I intervals are internally inconsistent beyond the one the card flags (editors' calculation, t(11) = 2.201, n = 12): amphetamine AUC0-t after 0.25 mg/kg l-methamphetamine, 32.1 (SD 21.6) with interval 13.4-45.8, whose midpoint is 29.6 and half-width 16.2 against the 13.7 the SD implies; and amphetamine half-life after 0.5 mg/kg l-methamphetamine, 43.6 (SD 24.9) with interval 25.8-61.4, half-width 17.8 against 15.8. Every other interval in Table I reproduces exactly at n = 12.
